findings.reason: recasting §2 as "extend `install.py`'s composer/recogniser and delete cli.py's copies" removes invented work and points the implementer at the owner.
findings.text: §2 proposes "one composer writes every reckon hook command" and "one recogniser … bare or bound" as though new, but `build_hook_snippet` (install.py:140) already composes every command as `interpreter_path()` (install.py:124, `.venv/bin/python`) followed by the script, `_command_identity` (install.py:414) already treats the bare and bound forms of a hook as one entry, `_merge_settings` (install.py:307) already upgrades a bare command in place, and `tests/test_hook_installer.py:246` already proves a worker stop hook and git guard decide correctly under a broken `python3` on PATH, with :449, :471 and :568 covering the bare-form upgrade and the untouched real settings file; the plan's §2 done-when items therefore largely restate behaviour that ships and is tested.

findings.reason: naming one owner for the shim, or stating the bootstrap reason it cannot be shared, decides whether §4 is one module or five copied blocks.
findings.text: §4 says "Each reckon hook script therefore checks … when it cannot [serve it] re-executes itself", which replicates one bootstrap shim inline in up to five scripts (coordinator_obligations.py, worker_stop.py, worker_git_guard.py, native_agent_guard.py, worker_message_guard.py) rather than one shared stdlib-only fragment; a shared by-path/vendored shim is possible (the check is pre-import, so it need not import reckon), yet the plan neither proposes a single home for the shim nor states why the duplication is forced, so the complexity is spread across shallow copies.

findings.reason: scoping §4's re-exec to the scripts that import reckon, stating why the stdlib-only guards are exempt, keeps a working guard working.
findings.text: §4's "Each reckon hook script" reaches `native_agent_guard.py` and `worker_message_guard.py`, whose own docstrings state they are "Self-contained and stdlib-only on purpose … never import from `reckon`", and which §1 of the plan itself says decide correctly under 3.9; adding a re-exec that redirects them to a checkout's `.venv/bin/python` contradicts that distribution design, since these guards ship into repositories that carry no reckon environment, and their §4 done-when only asks that they "decide unchanged".

findings.reason: without naming these sites the "one recogniser" claim is unfixed and a second, bare, writer remains beside the composer.
findings.text: the plan's "one composer … one recogniser … both writers use it" never names the duplicate machinery in `reckon sync`'s writer `_configure_crew_guards` (cli.py:413), which emits bare commands (`shlex.join([str(_native_agent_guard_path())])` at cli.py:472 and cli.py:483), carries two recognisers that duplicate install.py's (`_is_native_agent_guard_group` cli.py:318, `_is_worker_message_guard_group` cli.py:343) beside the one it already delegates (`_is_worker_git_guard_group` cli.py:368), and re-implements the atomic settings write (`_write_json_atomically` cli.py:373) that install.py's `_write_settings` (install.py:445) owns. The owner to extend is `reckon/hooks/install.py`; the sites to retire are cli.py:318,343,373,472,483, and the tests asserting the bare form they produce (`tests/test_guard_install.py`:126,176) must move with them.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §4 spreads one self-correction shim across every hook script instead of one shared bootstrap, adding surface without depth.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan says "one composer … one recogniser" without naming the parallel writer and two duplicate recognisers in `reckon/cli.py` that must be retired, or the owner to extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1589, cli_options 336, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; no section adds a public definition, CLI option, MCP view or `format_refusal` family (§5 reuses the existing `hooks install --write`), so nothing needs retiring or merging.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's §2 composer, bare-or-bound recogniser and in-place upgrade already exist in `reckon/hooks/install.py` and are already exercised by `tests/test_hook_installer.py`, but the plan cites none of them and so reads as new construction.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4 adds a re-exec wrapper to `native_agent_guard.py` and `worker_message_guard.py`, which import no reckon module and whose stated design is to be self-contained.
